Expectation1: Maintain regular communication with family members
Situation1: A family member has a new job and has shared some initial excitement about it with their relatives.
Expectation2: Communicate with clients and vendors regarding financial matters.
Situation2: A vendor sent a standard automated confirmation of a recent payment, to which a formal reply should be sent.
Story: I sat at my desk, the soft ping of my phone drawing my attention away from the spreadsheet on my computer. My daughter had just texted the family group chat, bubbling with excitement about her new job. I knew she expected me to respond quickly, to share in her joy and offer the encouragement she always looked for from me. At the same time, my email inbox flashed with a new message—a vendor’s automated payment confirmation. As an accountant, I was expected to reply promptly and formally, keeping our professional relationships smooth and reliable. I could feel the pressure mounting, the tug of family warmth on one side and professional duty on the other. My fingers hovered over the keyboard, my mind racing with the competing demands. I wanted to be present for my family, to show them they mattered, but I also knew the importance of maintaining my reputation at work. The seconds ticked by, and I felt the weight of both roles pressing in, each expecting my immediate attention.
